source.title: The Flow Associated to Weakly Differentiable Vector Fields: Recent Results and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let b(t,x)=b_t(x):(0,T)×R^d→R^d be a bounded possibly nonautonomous Borel velocity field, and consider the continuity equation ∂_t w_t + ∇·(b_t w_t)=0. Which assumptions on b ensure existence and uniqueness of nonnegative solutions in L^∞([0,T]; L^1(R^d) ∩ L^∞(R^d))?

evidence.quote: Here b(t, x) = bt(x) : (0, T) × R^d → R^d is a possibly nonautonomous Borel velocity field in R^d.
The main question is: which assumptions on b ensure that (1.1) has existence and uniqueness in L∞+[0, T];L1 ∩ L∞(Rd)?

accepted.question_text: Does the existence-and-uniqueness theory for the continuity equation and the associated regular Lagrangian flow extend from BV- and LD-type assumptions to vector fields in BD, where BD is the space of functions u such that the symmetric distributional derivative Du + tDu is representable by a measure?

evidence.quote: Recall that BD consists in the space of functions u such that (Du + tDu) are representable by measures.
The extension to BD vector fields is still an open problem

accepted.question_text: Suppose the vector field has the singular-integral form b_t(x)=∫_{R^d} K(x-y)F_t(y)dy, where K is a standard singular-integral kernel. Can the corresponding well-posedness and flow theory be extended from the case F_t∈L^1(R^d)^d to the case where F_t is merely a measure? Such an extension would cover BV vector fields and even BD vector fields through the same elliptic-PDE representation argument discussed in the source.

evidence.quote: Recently Bouchut and Crippa achieved in [24] a very nice extension of the theory to vector fields bt that can be represented as a singular integral bt(x) = ∫Rd K(x − y)Ft(y) dy with Ft ∈ [L1(Rd)]d.

In this direction, it would be very nice to have an extension of this result to the case when Ft is just a measure, and not necessarily an L1 function. This would include BV and even BD vectorfields, by the same elliptic PDE argument illustrated above.

accepted.question_text: Assume there is a nonnegative density ρ satisfying ∂_tρ_t + ∇·(b_tρ_t)=0. When b_t belongs to BV and ρ belongs to L^∞, does one have uniqueness of the associated flow and well-posedness of the corresponding partial differential equation relative to the reference measure ρ·L^d?
accepted.context_brief: BV fields with weighted reference density

evidence.quote: More generally, we may think that whenever we have a nonnegative function ρ satisfying ∂tρt + ∇ · (btρt) = 0 (3.1) then we should think to ρLd as our new reference measure and try to obtain well-posedness, at least in the regions where ρ does not vanish.
The uniqueness of the flow and the well-posedness of the PDE when bt ∈ BV and the function ρ in (3.1) belongs to L∞ are still open problems

accepted.question_text: Let X(t,x) be the L^d-regular Lagrangian flow associated to a nonsmooth vector field b. In the W^{1,1} case one knows that, for almost every t, there exists a measurable matrix-valued map W_t(x) such that the difference quotients (X(t,x+εy)-X(t,x))/ε converge locally in measure to W_t(x)y as ε↓0. Does this derivative-in-measure property remain valid for BV vector fields?
accepted.context_brief: Differentiability in measure of the flow

evidence.quote: Then for a.e. t ∈ (0, T) there exists a measurable function Wt : Rd → Md×d such that (X(t, x + εy) − X(t, x))/ε → Wt(x)y locally in measure in Rdx × Rdy as ε ↓ 0, uniformly in time.
(4.1) is the only differentiability property known in the W1,1 case, and unknown in the BV case.

accepted.question_text: Let ν be a regular measure on P(R^d), meaning that its expectation Eν is bounded above by C·L^d for some constant C. Can there exist a ν-regular Lagrangian flow μ in P(R^d) that is not induced by any L^d-regular Lagrangian flow X in R^d via the formula μ(t,μ)=∫_{R^d} δ_{X(t,x)} dμ(x)?

evidence.quote: We say that ν ∈ M+(P(Rd)) is regular if Eν ≤ CLd for some constant C.
one may speculate about situations where a ν-RLF µ exists in P(Rd), with ν regular, but the flow µ is not induced by any Ld-RLF X as in (5.3).
